text:
maria: Quick heads-up: pushed a smoke autotune run for candidate kernels on ampere-midseq. kbench sampler flagged a 12% p95 regression vs baseline on seqlen 1024. Anyone else see this? I'll attach logs.

perf-bot: kbench-run-2248009876 finished · artifacts: https://ci.redwood/arch/2248009876/logs.tar.gz :rocket:

alex: Can you paste the microbench command and the kernel pick table? also which config (batching/kv) used?

maria: cmd: `./kbench --model gpt2-like --seqlen 1024 --trials 100 --kernels candidate_set_v3 --batch-strat dynamic`

maria: config snippet:
```
batching:
  strategy: dynamic
  dynamic_threshold: 32
kv_cache:
  enabled: true
  prefix_caching: false
scoring:
  latency_weight: 0.7
  throughput_weight: 0.3
```

kai: Is KV cache enabled? we saw caching changes can flip midseq picks.

maria: KV cache: enabled, prefix caching disabled. Batching heuristics: 'dynamic' threshold 32 tokens. Candidate kernel that regressed: kernel_id=0x4f3b ('fused-attn-v2') baseline was 'fused-attn-v1'.

jen: Could be path-specific kernel selection; try forcing arch-aware pick for Ampere and re-run with `--force-kernel fused-attn-v1`.

alex: Also run with `--sample-weight seqlen-dist=production.json` to reflect real traffic. previous autotune used uniform seqlen, which overweights 1024.

maria: Re-ran with forced kernel + production seqlen weight: p95 back to baseline. So autotune scoring is overfitting to the microbench distribution. Suggest: add seqlen-aware penalty to candidate scoring.

kai: :thumbsup: +1. Maybe adjust cost model to include KV cache miss/hit ratio and batching tail latency.

jen: We should add a nightly sweep variant 'seq-aware' that uses prod seqlen histogram and KV model. I'll open a PR to harness.

maria: Created PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kbench/pull/412 — includes sampling plug-in and new scoring weight. Perf-bot will schedule a nightly on 01:00 UTC.

perf-bot: job scheduled: nightly-kbench-seq-aware · next run 01:00 UTC · ticket: #987

alex: Nice. Also note CI flakiness: one run had GPU thermal throttle; logs show power cap warnings. We should add a pre-check in harness to bail on thermal events.

maria: Good catch. Adding pre-check to detect `nvidia-smi --query -e ...` ??? Actually logs snippet: `GPU 0: throttle_warning: 0x42`

jen: Ok I'll add an infra check and a retry policy (max 2).

kai: For tracking: write a small regression test: run baseline vs candidate on seqlen buckets [1-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024] and record p95/p50.

maria: Agreed. I'll produce a compact artifact CSV in the run: `kbench_summary.csv`.

alex: Thanks team. Let's monitor nightly; if seq-aware picks diverge from cost-model-opt picks, we need to update optimize suggestions too.
